s0101.literal: " On yisi day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.
s0101.idiomatic: On yisi day the emperor personally sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.

s0102.literal: On jiachen day, General Who Quells the Distance and Liangzhou Inspector Zhang Li memorialized that in the eighth month of the year before last, yihai, [11] on the flank of a remnant mountain at the border of Dantu and Lanling commanderies, all at once because of surging tide-waters sand piled up, circling more than a thousand qing, all fertile and fit for opening to cultivation.
s0102.idiomatic: On jiachen day Zhang Li, general who quells the distance and Liangzhou inspector, reported that in the eighth month two years before, [11] beside a remnant hill on the border of Dantu and Lanling, tidal flood had suddenly thrown up sand over a thousand qing of rich soil fit for cultivation.

s0103.literal: On wuwu day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
s0103.idiomatic: On wuwu day the emperor personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

s0104.literal: In the second month, on renshen day, South Yuzhou Inspector Shen Tai fled to Qi.
s0104.idiomatic: In the second month, on renshen day, Shen Tai, inspector of South Yuzhou, defected to Qi.

s0105.literal: [12] On xinmao day an edict ordered Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister of Works Hou Tian to take overall command of the water and land combined armies to check the Qi invaders.
s0105.idiomatic: [12] On xinmao day an edict placed Hou Tian, grand general of chariots and cavalry and minister of works, in overall command of naval and land forces to block the Qi invasion.

s0106.literal: In the third month, on jiawu day, an edict said: "Punishment does not reach the sons—this is an ancient universal canon; when guilt is doubtful, lean toward leniency—it is set forth in the statutes.
s0106.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu day, an edict declared: "Punishment does not fall on heirs—so the ancients taught; when guilt is in doubt, favor mercy—so the law books say."

s0107.literal: Shen Tai was fickle and without conduct, known far and near. In the past he had slight merit and still bore the court's trust; with divided tally he held a famed commandery, with chariot-shaft he was pushed up through many border posts. When the army withdrew from Hankou he returned to a territorial post. Good fields exceeded four hundred; retainers numbered no fewer than three thousand—wealth, honor, and glory ought indeed to be thus.
s0107.idiomatic: Shen Tai was treacherous and faithless, known throughout the realm. He had once done minor service and still held the court's trust; enfeoffed in a great commandery, promoted through many frontier posts. After the Hankou campaign he returned to provincial command. His estates ran to four hundred fields; his retainers to three thousand—such were the rewards of his rank."

s0108.literal: Ghosts harmed his fullness; Heaven took his soul. Without cause he ran wild and threw himself among the savage foes.
s0108.idiomatic: His pride invited ruin; Heaven withdrew his wits. Without provocation he rebelled and cast himself among the barbarians."

s0109.literal: Though again to know men is wise and only the emperor finds it hard—Guangwu was blinded regarding Pang Meng; Weiwu did not know Yu Jin—only let the court have no case of Our failing others.
s0109.idiomatic: Even the wise err in judging men—only an emperor finds it hardest. Guangwu was deceived by Pang Meng; Cao Cao misread Yu Jin. Let the court never say We wronged Our servants."

s0110.literal: His troops' wives and children are each ordered to resume their occupations. Wherever soldiers have intimidated or plundered, all are to be prosecuted as bandits.
s0110.idiomatic: His soldiers' families shall return to their trades. Any trooper who threatens or loots the people shall be punished as a brigand."

s0111.literal: If any men or women are hidden by others, all are permitted to come to the capital to appeal.
s0111.idiomatic: Anyone held in secret bondage may appeal at court."

s0112.literal: If any wish to follow the King of Linchuan and the commanders bearing staffs to render merit, all are permitted.
s0112.idiomatic: Those who wish to serve the King of Linchuan or other commanders in earning merit may do so."

s0113.literal: " On yimao day the Founder visited the rear hall to hear lawsuits; returning, on the bridge he viewed mountains and waters and composed a poem to show the assembled ministers.
s0113.idiomatic: On yimao day the Founder heard cases in the rear hall; on his way back he paused on the bridge to take in the landscape and wrote a poem for his ministers.

s0114.literal: That month Wang Lin installed Liang's Prince of Yongjia, Xiao Zhuang, at Yingzhou.
s0114.idiomatic: That month Wang Lin set up Xiao Zhuang, Prince of Yongjia of Liang, at Yingzhou.

s0115.literal: In the sixth month, on jisi day, an edict ordered Minister of Works Hou Tian and Palace Bulwark General Xu Du to lead the fleet as the vanguard army to attack Wang Lin.
s0115.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jisi day, an edict ordered Hou Tian, minister of works, and Xu Du, palace bulwark general, to lead the fleet as vanguard against Wang Lin.

s0116.literal: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the imperial carriage went to Stone City and personally sent off Tian and the others.
s0116.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the emperor went to Stone City and personally saw off Hou Tian and the commanders.

s0117.literal: On jihai day Jiangzhou Inspector Zhou Di captured Wang Lin's generals Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang at Gongtang.
s0117.idiomatic: On jihai day Zhou Di, inspector of Jiangzhou, took Wang Lin's generals Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang at Gongtang.

s0118.literal: On jiachen day the Minister of Personnel Xie Zhe was sent to instruct Wang Lin.
s0118.idiomatic: On jiachen day Xie Zhe, minister of personnel, was dispatched to address Wang Lin.

s0119.literal: On jiayin day at Wucheng a single stalk of grain with six tines grew.
s0119.idiomatic: On jiayin day a six-tined ear of grain appeared at Wucheng.

s0120.literal: Earlier, when Hou Jing was pacified, fire had burned the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate. In the Chengsheng era deliberation wished to rebuild it, but alone one pillar was lacking. Now there was a camphor tree eighteen arm-spans around and four zhang five chi long, drifting to moor at the rear ford of the Tao household. Supervising general Zou Zidu reported it.
s0120.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fell, fire had destroyed the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate. Under Emperor Chengsheng the court planned to rebuild it but lacked a single pillar. Now a camphor eighteen spans around and four zhang five chi long drifted to the Tao family's rear landing; the supervising general Zou Zidu reported it.

s0121.literal: An edict ordered Central Secretariat Director Shen Zhong also to serve as Director of the Ministry that Raises Works, and Junior Chamberlain for the Palace Treasury Cai Chou also to serve as Director of Works, to raise the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
s0121.idiomatic: An edict named Shen Zhong, director of the central secretariat, concurrent director of the ministry that raises works, and Cai Chou, junior chamberlain for the palace treasury, concurrent director of works, to rebuild the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

s0122.literal: In the eighth month, on yingyin day, Guangliang commandery was made Chenliu commandery.
s0122.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yingyin day, Guangliang commandery was renamed Chenliu.

s0123.literal: On xinwei day an edict ordered the King of Linchuan, Qian, on the western campaign; [13] with a fleet of fifty thousand he set out from the capital, and the imperial carriage went to Ye City Monastery to see him off in person.
s0123.idiomatic: On xinwei day an edict sent the King of Linchuan, Qian, on the western campaign. [13] With fifty thousand sailors he sailed from the capital, and the emperor went in person to Ye City Monastery to see him off.

s0124.literal: Former Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and South Yuzhou Inspector Zhou Wenyü, and former General Who Pacifies the North, South Xuzhou Inspector, and newly appointed Grand Mentor with Staff Hou Andu, who had escaped from Wang Lin's custody, impeached themselves before the Court for Punishments; that same day they were received in audience and all were pardoned.
s0124.idiomatic: Zhou Wenyü, former grand mentor with staff and inspector of South Yuzhou, and Hou Andu, former general who pacifies the north, inspector of South Xuzhou, and newly made grand mentor with staff, who had escaped Wang Lin, presented themselves to the court of punishments to confess fault; that day they were received and pardoned.

s0125.literal: On wuyin day an edict restored Wenyü and the others to their former offices.
s0125.idiomatic: On wuyin day an edict restored Wenyü and the others to their former posts.

s0126.literal: On renwu day the Founder's son Li was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Yuzhang, posthumous name Xian;
s0126.idiomatic: On renwu day the Founder's son Li was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Yuzhang, posthumous name Xian;

s0127.literal: Quan as King of Changsha, posthumous name Si;
s0127.idiomatic: Quan as King of Changsha, posthumous name Si;

s0128.literal: the eldest daughter as Princess of Eternal Generations, posthumous name Yi.
s0128.idiomatic: and the eldest daughter as Princess of Eternal Generations, posthumous name Yi.

s0129.literal: Xie Zhe returned with a contrary mandate. Wang Lin asked to return and hold Xiang River; an edict recalled the armies and suspended the campaign.
s0129.idiomatic: Xie Zhe returned without agreement. Wang Lin asked to withdraw to the Xiang; an edict recalled the armies and halted the offensive.

s0130.literal: On guiwei day the western campaign armies arrived from Great Thunder.
s0130.idiomatic: On guiwei day the western expedition reached Great Thunder.

s0131.literal: On dinghai day the Trustworthy and Martial General and Jiangzhou Inspector Zhou Di was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.
s0131.idiomatic: On dinghai day Zhou Di, trustworthy and martial general and inspector of Jiangzhou, was made grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes and promoted to general who pacifies the south.

s0132.literal: South Lanling commandery under South Xuzhou was again made Donghai commandery.
s0132.idiomatic: South Lanling commandery under South Xuzhou was restored as Donghai.

s0133.literal: In the tenth month, on gengwu day, Pacifying South General and Grand Mentor with Staff Zhou Wenyü was sent as commander-in-chief of the armies to march out of Yuzhang to attack Yu Xiaoxiang.
s0133.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on gengwu day, Zhou Wenyü, pacifying south general and grand mentor with staff, was sent from Yuzhang at the head of the armies against Yu Xiaoxiang.

s0134.literal: On yihai day the imperial carriage visited Zhuangyan Monastery and opened the lecture on the Sutra of Golden Light.
s0134.idiomatic: On yihai day the emperor went to Zhuangyan Monastery to inaugurate the lecture on the Sutra of Golden Light.

s0135.literal: On dingyou day the Benevolent and Martial General and Gaozhou Inspector Huang Fa Tu was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes [14] and promoted to General Who Guards the South.
s0135.idiomatic: On dingyou day Huang Fa Tu, benevolent and martial general and inspector of Gaozhou, was made grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes [14] and promoted to general who guards the south.

s0136.literal: [15] On jiayin day the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate was completed; each craftsman was given exemption from corvée.
s0136.idiomatic: [15] On jiayin day the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate was finished; every craftsman was granted tax and labor exemption.

s0137.literal: On gengshen day the Palace Attendant and Pacifying East General, the King of Linchuan Qian, led the hundred offices to the front hall of the palace to bow and present oxen and wine.
s0137.idiomatic: On gengshen day Qian, king of Linchuan, palace attendant and pacifying east general, led the hundred offices to the front hall to offer oxen and wine.

s0138.literal: On jiazi day the imperial carriage visited the Great Zhuangyan Monastery and held an unbounded great assembly, donating the imperial carriage and ritual objects.
s0138.idiomatic: On jiazi day the emperor went to the Great Zhuangyan Monastery for a boundless great assembly and gave up the imperial carriage and ritual regalia.

s0139.literal: The assembled ministers with full ritual carriages came to welcome him; that same day the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
s0139.idiomatic: Ministers with full ceremonial escort came to welcome him; that day the emperor returned to the palace.

s0140.literal: On yingyin day the Founder at the eastern hall of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate feasted the assembled ministers and set out metal and stone music, because the inner chamber dwelling was reported complete.
s0140.idiomatic: On yingyin day the Founder feasted his ministers in the eastern hall of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate with full orchestra, celebrating completion of the inner palace.

s0141.literal: On renshen day from Wu commandery's Yanguan, Haiyan, and Qianjing counties Haining commandery was established, subordinate to Yangzhou.
s0141.idiomatic: On renshen day Haining commandery was carved from Yanguan, Haiyan, and Qianjing in Wu commandery and placed under Yangzhou.

s0142.literal: From Ancheng's six caves of Guangxing, Anle commandery was established.
s0142.idiomatic: From the six caves of Guangxing in Ancheng, Anle commandery was established.

s0143.literal: On jingxu day the Pacifying Distance General and North Jiangzhou Inspector Xiong Tanlang was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
s0143.idiomatic: On jingxu day Xiong Tanlang, pacifying distance general and inspector of North Jiangzhou, was made grand mentor with staff and promoted to general who pacifies the west.

s0144.literal: On dinghai day an edict said: "Former Liang officials, scattered by disorder, have only lately returned to court and for the most part have not yet been ranked.
s0144.idiomatic: On dinghai day an edict declared: "Former officials of Liang, scattered by the troubles, have only now returned to court and for the most part await appointment."

s0145.literal: Since the raising of armies, military merit has been very numerous.
s0145.idiomatic: Since the armies were raised, military merit has been abundant."

s0146.literal: The Selection Office is immediately to list civil and military registers and commanders bearing staffs who fit the nine ranks, and weigh what posts suit them.
s0146.idiomatic: The Selection Office shall at once compile rolls of civil and military men and of commanders with staffs eligible for the nine ranks, and assign posts as their talents warrant."

s0147.literal: " Thereupon more than fifty men were promoted according to ability.
s0147.idiomatic: More than fifty men were then promoted according to ability.

s0148.literal: In the third year, first month, on jichou day, a green dragon appeared in the east.
s0148.idiomatic: In the third year, first month, on jichou day, a green dragon was seen in the east.

s0149.literal: On dingyou day the General Who Guards the South and Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei was given his present title as Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
s0149.idiomatic: On dingyou day Ouyang Wei, general who guards the south and inspector of Guangzhou, was confirmed as grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes.

s0150.literal: That night great snow fell, and at dawn dragon tracks were seen before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
s0150.idiomatic: That night heavy snow fell; by dawn dragon tracks appeared before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

s0151.literal: On jiawu day Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei memorialized that a white dragon appeared on the south bank south of the province, [16] several tens of zhang long and eight or nine arm-spans around, passing west along the provincial city road into Heavenly Well Ridge.
s0151.idiomatic: On jiawu day Ouyang Wei, inspector of Guangzhou, reported a white dragon on the south bank south of the city, [16] tens of zhang in length and eight or nine spans around, which passed west along the city road into Heavenly Well Ridge.

s0152.literal: An immortal appeared at the small stone tower of Luofu Mountain Monastery, about three zhang tall, all body pure white, garments splendid in Chu style.
s0152.idiomatic: An immortal was seen at the small stone tower on Luofu Mountain, some three zhang tall, wholly white, dressed in splendid Chu fashion.

s0153.literal: On xinchou day an edict said: "The younger sisters of the kings of Nankang and Shixing already have enfeoffments; by ritual they should only be feudal ladies.
s0153.idiomatic: On xinchou day an edict declared: "The younger sisters of the kings of Nankang and Shixing already hold titles; by ritual they should rank only as feudal princesses."

s0154.literal: These two kings have a special constant feeling; ritual measure ought to be exalted.
s0154.idiomatic: These two kings stand in a special bond; their sisters deserve higher honor."

s0155.literal: The princesses' ritual ranks and those who marry them may both be the same as imperial daughters.
s0155.idiomatic: Let the princesses' ceremonial standing and their husbands' ranks equal those of the emperor's own daughters."

s0156.literal: " On wushen day an edict ordered the King of Linchuan, Qian, to review lawsuits of Yang and Xu provinces.
s0156.idiomatic: On wushen day an edict charged the King of Linchuan, Qian, with hearing appeals from Yang and Xu provinces.

s0157.literal: In the second month, on xinyou day, the General Who Pacifies the West and Guizhou Inspector Chunyu Liang was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to Grand General Who Guards the West.
s0157.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinyou day, Chunyu Liang, general who pacifies the west and inspector of Guizhou, was made grand mentor with staff and promoted to grand general who guards the west.

s0158.literal: On renwu day Minister of Works Hou Tian commanded the armies from the river into Hefei and burned Qi's boats.
s0158.idiomatic: On renwu day Hou Tian, minister of works, led the armies from the Yangtze into Hefei and burned Qi's fleet.

s0159.literal: In the third month, on jingshen day, Hou Tian returned from Hefei; the armies presented the spoils.
s0159.idiomatic: In the third month, on jingshen day, Hou Tian returned from Hefei and the armies reported victory.

s0160.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of summer, on gengyin day, an edict said: "Opening granaries to relieve the destitute is the great bounty for nurturing the people; touring the regions to pity the afflicted is the former kings' established canon.
s0160.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of summer, on gengyin day, an edict declared: "Opening the granaries to save the starving is the great act of nurturing the people; touring the realm to ease suffering is the ancient kings' law."

s0161.literal: We meet this declining age and receive this joyful succession; Our lordly virtue is not yet trusted, the people's afflictions are still severe. Heaping ramparts upon ramparts, We are the more ashamed to stand at the brink.
s0161.idiomatic: "We came to power in a fallen age and accepted the people's acclaim, yet Our virtue has not won their hearts and their suffering remains deep. Fortress upon fortress of trouble fills Us with shame."

s0162.literal: Truly because the four keen listeners were not reached, [17] a thousand li gave no response.
s0162.idiomatic: Truly the four keen listeners were not heard, [17] and no voice answered from a thousand li."

s0163.literal: [18] The benevolence of broad giving—how could it ever fail?
s0163.idiomatic: [18] How could the grace of broad giving ever be wanting?"

s0164.literal: The track of ruin and exhaustion brought this not yet to peace.
s0164.idiomatic: Yet the road of ruin and exhaustion has not yet led to peace."

s0165.literal: Wu and Jing provinces last year suffered locusts and drought. Though the fields of Ying were charmed, [19] the Zheng Canal in the end dried up. Houses had no hope of full stores; families had the lament of filling gullies.
s0165.idiomatic: Wu and Jing provinces suffered locusts and drought last year. Though the fields of Ying were blessed, [19] the Zheng Canal ran dry at last. No household could hope for a full granary; many faced starvation."

s0166.literal: If the hundred surnames are not sufficient, on what do the myriad people rely?
s0166.idiomatic: When the people lack food, what can the realm depend upon?"

s0167.literal: Recently We have sent Palace Attendant Jiang Dezao bearing Our mandate to Dongyang to question the people and officials of two thousand piculs rank about their hardships, and likewise to divide and comfort them with rice from the capital granary on hand.
s0167.idiomatic: We have lately sent Jiang Dezao, palace attendant, to Dongyang with Our mandate to inquire into the people's hardships with the local magistrates, and to distribute grain from the capital granaries in relief."

s0168.literal: Though Our virtue is not yet that of full satiety, We hope in small measure to comfort those who block hunger.
s0168.idiomatic: Our virtue is not yet enough to fill every belly, yet We hope in some measure to ease those who starve."

s0169.literal: " On jiawu day an edict ordered, following former dynasties, Western Secretariat scholars established, and moreover those skilled in arts and techniques to be included.
s0169.idiomatic: On jiawu day an edict, following earlier dynasties, established scholars of the Western Secretariat, including men skilled in arts and techniques.

s0170.literal: On dingyou day Pacifying North General Xu Du led the armies south to Wan Estuary.
s0170.idiomatic: On dingyou day Xu Du, pacifying north general, led the armies south to Wan Estuary.

s0171.literal: At this time rain had long been lacking. On jingwu day the imperial carriage visited Zhongshan to sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Jiang; that day rain fell, continuing until the month's end.
s0171.idiomatic: Rain had long been absent. On jingwu day the emperor sacrificed at Emperor Jiang's temple on Zhongshan; rain fell that day and lasted to month's end.

s0172.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, jingchen, there was a solar eclipse. The relevant offices memorialized: According to old ritual, at the front hall one wears the vermilion gauze robe and the penetrating-heaven crown.
s0172.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month, jingchen, there was a solar eclipse. The relevant offices reported the old rite: at the front hall the emperor should wear the vermilion gauze robe and penetrating-heaven crown.

s0173.literal: An edict said: "This is what former generations used in succession; the intent is not the same.
s0173.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Former generations followed this practice, but the meaning is not the same."

s0174.literal: At the conjunction one looks up to aid the sun; one ought to prepare the robes of the full regalia.
s0174.idiomatic: At the conjunction one assists the sun; full imperial regalia should be worn."

s0175.literal: From now onward this shall forever be the standard.
s0175.idiomatic: Henceforth this shall be the permanent rule."

s0176.literal: " On yingyin day Funan sent envoys presenting local products.
s0176.idiomatic: On yingyin day Funan sent envoys with tribute.

s0177.literal: On yiyou day North Jiangzhou Inspector Xiong Tanlang killed Commander-in-Chief Zhou Wenyü in the army and raised troops in rebellion.
s0177.idiomatic: On yiyou day Xiong Tanlang, inspector of North Jiangzhou, murdered the commander Zhou Wenyü in camp and rebelled.

s0178.literal: Wang Lin sent his generals Chang Zhong'ai and Cao Qing leading troops to aid Yu Xiaoxiang.
s0178.idiomatic: Wang Lin sent his generals Chang Zhong'ai and Cao Qing with troops to support Yu Xiaoxiang.

s0179.literal: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Hou Andu defeated Zhong'ai and the others at Zuoli, capturing Wang Lin's younger cousin Xi, chief commander Yang Xian, and more than thirty others. Zhong'ai fled; on gengyin day the people of Lushan beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.
s0179.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Hou Andu, bearer of staff equal to the three dukes, routed Zhong'ai at Zuoli and took Wang Lin's cousin Xi, the commander Yang Xian, and more than thirty others. Zhong'ai fled; on gengyin day the people of Lushan killed him and sent his head to the capital.

s0180.literal: On jiawu day the armies returned in triumph.
s0180.idiomatic: On jiawu day the armies returned in triumph.

s0181.literal: An edict said: "Tanlang devoured and rebelled; his crime brooks no execution. We ordered the armies to continue the concealed attack; when he is exposed to the halter and cleaver, the penal statutes will be made clear.
s0181.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Tanlang has turned traitor and murderer; his crime admits no pardon. The armies are already hunting him; when he is taken, the law will be made plain."

s0182.literal: " The King of Linchuan, Qian, was summoned to Wan Estuary to set up stockades and palisades; Qian Daozai was left to defend them.
s0182.idiomatic: The King of Linchuan, Qian, was called to Wan Estuary to build fortifications, with Qian Daozai left to hold them.

s0183.literal: On dingyou day the Founder was unwell. He sent Concurrent Grand Minister of Sacrifices and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Tong to report the illness to the Grand Temple, and Concurrent Grand Minister of Sacrifices and Central Secretariat Director Xie Zhe to report to the Grand Altar and the southern and northern suburbs.
s0183.idiomatic: On dingyou day the Founder fell ill. He sent Wang Tong, concurrent grand minister of sacrifices and left vice director of the secretariat, to announce his illness at the Grand Temple, and Xie Zhe, concurrent grand minister of sacrifices and director of the central secretariat, to announce it at the Grand Altar and the suburban altars.

s0184.literal: On xinchou day the Founder's illness slightly improved.
s0184.idiomatic: On xinchou day the Founder's illness eased slightly.

s0185.literal: The coffin of the late Minister of Works Zhou Wenyü arrived from Jianchang.
s0185.idiomatic: The coffin of the late Zhou Wenyü, minister of works, arrived from Jianchang.

s0186.literal: On renyin day the Founder in plain robes wept in the eastern hall, grief extreme.
s0186.idiomatic: On renyin day the Founder, in plain mourning dress, wept in the eastern hall with deepest grief.

s0187.literal: On guimao day the Founder personally inspected and questioned at the pris
s0187.idiomatic: On guimao day the Founder personally heard prison cases.

s0190.literal: [20] That night the Sparkling Deluder was at the Celestial Honored One.
s0190.idiomatic: [20] That night Mars stood at the Celestial Honored One.

s0191.literal: The Founder's illness again grew severe.

s0192.literal: [21] On jingwu day he died at the Hall of the Rotating Pearl, aged fifty-seven.
s0192.idiomatic: [21] On jingwu day he died in the Hall of the Rotating Pearl, aged fifty-seven.

s0193.literal: The testamentary edict recalled the King of Linchuan, Qian, to succeed.
s0193.idiomatic: His testament summoned the King of Linchuan, Qian, to succeed him.

s0194.literal: On jiayin day the late emperor's coffin was moved to lie in state at the western steps of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
s0194.idiomatic: On jiayin day the late emperor's coffin was placed in state at the western steps of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

s0195.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, the assembled ministers posthumously titled him Emperor Wu, temple name Founder.
s0195.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, the ministers gave him the posthumous title Emperor Wu and the temple name Founder.

s0196.literal: On jingshen day he was buried at Wan'an Tomb.
s0196.idiomatic: On jingshen day he was buried at Wan'an Tomb.

s0197.literal: The Founder with wisdom pacified things, with martial prowess settled disorder; his heroic stratagem worked alone—none could match him. Therefore he could conquer on campaign in four directions and quiet hardship and level the fierce.
s0197.idiomatic: The Founder pacified the realm through wisdom and quelled chaos through arms; his strategy was his alone, and none could rival it. Thus he conquered in every direction and stilled rebellion and slaughter.

s0198.literal: When he ascended the great footstool's day he occupied the office of Aheng; he constantly honored lenient government and took cherishing nurture as the root.
s0198.idiomatic: Once he took the throne he held the burden of chief minister to the realm; he always favored lenient rule and made cherishing the people his foundation.

s0199.literal: Whenever it was necessary to issue levies for army stores, all arose from affairs that could not rest.
s0199.idiomatic: Whenever he levied grain for the armies, it was only because necessity would not allow rest.

s0200.literal: Moreover he led by frugal simplicity himself; ordinary meals were no more than a few dishes. Private feasts and informal banquets all used earthenware and clam shells for dishes; meat and vegetables were only enough to suffice—not for empty waste.
s0200.idiomatic: He was frugal in his own habits: daily meals were only a few courses; private feasts used pottery and clam shells, with food no more than enough—never spent on display.
